thread:
Alex: Quick sec question — we need to give on-call/support ephemeral console access to view prod customer logs when debugging incidents. Prefer short-lived sessions (JIT). What's the minimum role set you'd recommend and safe session duration? Also any must-have audit/redaction steps? Example flow: user impersonates support-sa for 15m.

Maya: Short answer: use service-account impersonation + logging viewer perms. Give the user `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on the support SA and bind `roles/logging.viewer` at the project (or narrower) scope to the SA. 15m is OK for a lot of cases, but 1h max is sometimes easier for longer debug. Recommend 15m for high-risk tenants. :thumbsup:

Sam: A couple of concrete notes:
- Prefer binding the viewer role to the SA at the project/tenant resource level, not org-wide.
- Add an IAM Condition on the SA impersonation binding to limit by time/window or by source IP where possible. Example condition expression (GCP):

```
title: "JIT support window"
condition: {
  expression: "request.time < timestamp(\"2026-03-17T16:30:00Z\") && request.auth.claims.email.endsWith('@redwood.com')",
  description: "limit token creation to a short window for approved users"
}
```

And example gcloud to allow impersonation: 

```
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding support-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member='user:alex@redwood.com' --role='roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator'
```

Then the SA would have `roles/logging.viewer` scoped to the customer project: 

```
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding customer-prod-project --member='serviceAccount:support-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/logging.viewer'
```

Maya: Also consider these operational controls:
- JIT approval workflow before impersonation (Slack/Okta ticket or support portal).
- Automation to record the approval ID in the impersonation audit log.
- Require MFA for token creators.
- Limit token TTL to 15m by default; allow escalation to 1h with manager approval.

Dave: For log redaction: ensure logging sinks redact PII before they hit the support-visible bucket. We have two levers: log exclusion filters at ingestion, and computed fields that mask values. Ask infra to verify the customer's prod logging pipeline masks `user_email`, `credit_card`, `ssn`. If those aren't masked, do not grant access until mitigations are in place.

security-bot: Policy check results (quick): support-sa currently has `roles/logging.viewer` in 1 customer project and `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` granted to group `support@redwood.com` at org level — that's too broad. Recommend moving `tokenCreator` to an allow-list of specific groups/users and add an IAM Condition for `resource.name` matching customer projects.

Alex: Good call on tokenCreator being org-wide. Can we do a quick PR to narrow it? I can open a small change to move `support@redwood.com` binding to the team JIT group and add a condition restricting `resource.name.startsWith('projects/customer-')`. Who can pair on the PR? @Maya?

Maya: I can pair after lunch. I'll draft the IAM condition and a short runbook for on-call. Also will add a note to require a support ticket ID in the impersonation reason field so audit logs show it.

Sam: I can do a config scan after the change and verify no org-wide `tokenCreator` remains. I'll also add an alert if any un-redacted log fields are present for prod.

Alex: Thanks all — I'll file the PR and tag you. If we want to block access until redaction is confirmed, say so here and I'll hold the change.

Dave: Block until infra confirms masking for the high-risk customer buckets. Otherwise proceed for low-risk tenants only.

Maya: Ack. I'll coordinate infra for the masking check and post back in this thread with the runbook draft.

security-bot: NOTE: all impersonation events are logged to `audit.logs` — include `protoPayload.methodName` and `authenticationInfo.principalEmail` in your review checklist.
